featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very mixed experience at this hospital. I visited the emergency department at 5:00 AM, and at that time, the staff and doctors were professional, supportive, and handled the situation very well.
However, my experience on the following day (between 4:00 PM and 5:00 PM) was absolutely appalling. The staff’s behavior was shocking and completely unacceptable
The staff members were arguing loudly with each other, creating a chaotic environment
When we politely asked if the patient could feed the baby, the staff responded with extreme rudeness, asking, "Why, haven't you fed the child before?"
The staff was arguing over who should document the medication and IV administration, with one person stating, "It’s not my patient, why should I write it?" They wasted 40–45 minutes of our time, and we had to insist repeatedly before they finally did their job.
At the reception, we faced further delays in getting our final bill. When my husband requested them to hurry up due to time constraints, the receptionist was incredibly rude. She used unprofessional language like "Chal hatt" (move away) and mockingly asked if we wanted free treatment. It is common sense that if someone didn’t want to pay, they wouldn't choose to visit a private hospital in the first place.
It feels like the staff and doctors have no concern for the patient’s well-being. Even government hospitals offer better, more empathetic service than what I witnessed here. I am deeply disappointed by the lack of discipline and the toxic behavior of the staff.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Kind att TPA TEAM
MIRA MULTISPECIALITY HOSPITAL.
BHAYANDAR WEST

I am extremely disappointed with the TPA service at Mira Multispeciality Hospital. A very similar issue had already happened earlier with one of my relatives, where the TPA team was repeatedly instructed nearly five times to scan and submit the doctor’s first prescription along with the required documents to the mediclaim company. Despite repeated reminders, they failed to do so, and because of their negligence, the claim was rejected.

Now the exact same mistake has happened again in my mother’s case while I am currently at the hospital. The physician had clearly prescribed and documented her medical condition, but the TPA team again failed to send the doctor’s initial prescription and proper documents to the insurance company on time. Because of this negligence, a query was raised by the mediclaim company asking for additional clarification and documents.

Even after the query was raised, the response from the TPA department was extremely casual. They simply said that it would take more time and that they could not process it immediately. Shockingly, they finally applied for the approval only around 5:00 PM on Saturday evening, fully aware that Sunday is a non-working day for many insurance processing departments. Due to this delay, the entire approval process has now been unnecessarily pushed ahead.

This does not look like a small accidental mistake anymore. When the same negligence happens repeatedly in multiple cases, it naturally creates doubt that these delays are being done intentionally so that the hospital billing cycle increases and patients are forced to stay longer, resulting in additional financial burden.

My mother is medically fit right now and ready for discharge. If the TPA team had submitted the doctor’s prescription and documents properly and on time, there would most likely have been no unnecessary query from the insurance company, and the mediclaim process would have been completed smoothly without any issue.

Because of this delay, my entire travel plan is now at risk. My mother has a flight scheduled on Monday, and if discharge gets delayed until sunday afternoon, it will become extremely difficult for us to reach the airport on time. If we miss the flight, I may suffer a loss of nearly ₹40,000. The question is — who will bear this loss caused purely due to the negligence and delay from the TPA department?

I am financially capable of managing this situation somehow, but I genuinely feel worried thinking about what ordinary families might go through in such situations. Many people may not have the financial strength, resources, or confidence to handle this kind of unnecessary stress and delay.

Money is not everything. Hospitals and TPA teams are dealing with patients and families during emotionally difficult times. Basic responsibility, honesty, and humanity are expected. I sincerely request the concerned people to fear God and understand the impact of their actions on patients and families.

As Lord Krishna teaches, every person’s time eventually comes, and whatever we do in this world must ultimately be faced and repaid here itself. We live our lives with this belief and understanding.

God sees everything. 🙏🙏
